_comment: Bird details shown on the site. 'name' is the canonical common name; Flickr titles are matched against name + aliases ignoring case, hyphens and extra spaces. When a new species is photographed, the sync asks Claude to write its entry and adds it here marked "auto" with the date; review those and edit freely (the sync never overwrites existing entries). Delete the "auto" field once you've checked one.

species.name: Baltimore Oriole
species.about: A flame-orange and black songbird that weaves a hanging, sock-like nest.

species.name: Common Grackle
species.about: A long-tailed blackbird with an iridescent purple-bronze sheen and pale yellow eyes.

species.name: Grayish Baywing
species.about: A gray-brown blackbird with rufous wings that often nests in other birds' old nests.

species.name: Red-winged Blackbird
species.about: A marsh blackbird; males display red and yellow shoulder patches and sing 'conk-la-ree!'

species.name: Shiny Cowbird
species.about: A glossy purple-black brood parasite that lays its eggs in other birds' nests.

species.name: Yellow-headed Blackbird
species.about: A marsh blackbird of the West with a vivid yellow head; its song sounds like a rusty gate.

species.name: Indigo Bunting
species.about: Males look vivid blue; the color comes from feather structure scattering light, not from pigment.

species.name: Lazuli Bunting
species.about: A western bunting; males are turquoise-blue with an orange breast and white wing bars.

species.name: Northern Cardinal
species.about: A crested songbird; the male is brilliant red. Both sexes sing.

species.name: Rose-breasted Grosbeak
species.about: Males have a rose-red triangle on a white breast and sing a robin-like song.

species.name: Scarlet Tanager
species.about: Breeding males are bright scarlet with black wings; the bird stays high in the forest canopy.

species.name: Double-crested Cormorant
species.about: A diving fish-eater often seen perched with its wings spread out to dry.

species.name: Neotropic Cormorant
species.about: A slim, long-tailed cormorant common across Central and South America.

species.name: Sandhill Crane
species.about: A tall gray crane with a red forehead and a rolling, bugling call. Has one of the longest fossil records of any living bird.

species.name: American Crow
species.about: A highly social and intelligent bird that can recognize individual human faces.

species.name: Blue Jay
species.about: A loud, intelligent jay that caches acorns and helps oak forests spread.

species.name: American Black Duck
species.about: A dark, Mallard-like duck of eastern marshes, with a purple-blue wing patch.

species.name: Black Scoter
species.about: An all-black sea duck (males have a knobby yellow-orange bill) that winters off Atlantic beaches.

species.name: Bufflehead
species.about: A tiny diving duck; males have a big white patch on an iridescent head.

species.name: Canada Goose
species.about: A large goose with a black neck and white chinstrap, common in parks and on lawns.

species.name: Cinnamon Teal
species.about: A small western duck; breeding males are a deep cinnamon-red with red eyes.

species.name: Gadwall
species.about: A subtly patterned gray-brown dabbling duck; it often steals food from diving ducks and coots.

species.name: Greater Scaup
species.about: A diving duck that winters in big rafts on coastal bays; males show a rounded, green-glossed head.

species.name: Hooded Merganser
species.about: A small fish-eating duck; the male raises and lowers a fan-shaped white crest.

species.name: Long-tailed Duck
species.about: A sea duck that can dive deeper than 60 m; males have long, slender tail plumes.

species.name: Mallard
species.about: The familiar ancestor of most domestic ducks; males have a glossy green head.

species.name: Muscovy Duck
species.about: A large tropical duck with red facial warts; widely domesticated and often feral in parks.

species.name: Mute Swan
species.about: A large white swan with an orange bill, introduced to North America from Europe.

species.name: Northern Shoveler
species.about: A dabbling duck with an oversized, spoon-shaped bill that it uses to strain food from the water.

species.name: Red-breasted Merganser
species.about: A fish-eating diving duck with a shaggy crest and a thin, serrated red bill.

species.name: Ring-necked Duck
species.about: A diving duck named for a faint chestnut neck ring that is hard to see; the white ring on its bill is easier.

species.name: Rosy-billed Pochard
species.about: A South American diving duck; males have a bright rose-red bill with a swollen knob at the base.

species.name: Ruddy Duck
species.about: A compact stiff-tailed duck; breeding males have a sky-blue bill.

species.name: Silver Teal
species.about: A South American dabbling duck with a blue bill, yellow at the base, and a pale cheek under a dark cap.

species.name: Wood Duck
species.about: A strikingly patterned duck that nests in tree cavities; ducklings leap from the nest within a day of hatching.

species.name: American Kestrel
species.about: North America's smallest falcon, often seen hovering over fields or perched on wires; it hunts insects, rodents and small birds.

species.name: Crested Caracara
species.about: A long-legged falcon that behaves like a hawk-vulture hybrid, walking the ground for prey and carrion.

species.name: Merlin
species.about: A compact, powerful falcon that ambushes small birds in fast, low flight. Increasingly common in cities and towns.

species.name: Peregrine Falcon
species.about: Famous for high-speed hunting stoops; recovered from DDT-era declines and now nests on bridges and skyscrapers.

species.name: American Goldfinch
species.about: A seed-eating finch; males turn bright yellow in summer. It nests late, timed to thistle seed.

species.name: Hooded Siskin
species.about: A goldfinch relative of South America; males have a black hood over yellow plumage.

species.name: House Finch
species.about: A western finch introduced to New York in the 1940s that has since spread across the East.

species.name: Horned Grebe
species.about: A small diving grebe; breeding adults have golden 'horns', while winter birds are crisp black and white.

species.name: Common Tern
species.about: A graceful tern that plunge-dives for small fish; it nests in colonies on beaches and islands.

species.name: Great Black-backed Gull
species.about: The largest gull in the world, with a black back and a powerful bill.

species.name: Herring Gull
species.about: The classic large 'seagull', with pink legs and a red spot on its yellow bill.

species.name: Laughing Gull
species.about: A summer gull of the Atlantic coast with a black hood and a laughing 'ha-ha-ha' call.

species.name: Ring-billed Gull
species.about: A medium-sized gull with a black ring around its bill, at home in parking lots as well as on beaches.

species.name: Bald Eagle
species.about: The US national bird. Adults get their white head and tail at about five years old; it feeds mostly on fish.

species.name: Cooper's Hawk
species.about: A crow-sized woodland hawk with a long, rounded tail. A frequent visitor to backyard feeders, where it hunts songbirds.

species.name: Golden Eagle
species.about: A huge eagle of open country with golden nape feathers that can dive at more than 240 km/h.

species.name: Harris's Hawk
species.about: A chocolate-and-chestnut hawk that hunts cooperatively in family groups; a favorite of falconers.

species.name: Northern Harrier
species.about: Glides low over marshes and fields with wings in a shallow V; has an owl-like facial disk for hunting by sound.

species.name: Red-shouldered Hawk
species.about: A vocal forest hawk with a barred rufous chest and checkered wings, usually near water.

species.name: Red-tailed Hawk
species.about: The most widespread hawk in North America, often perched along highways. Adults show a brick-red tail.

species.name: Sharp-shinned Hawk
species.about: The smallest North American hawk; a fast, agile hunter of small songbirds.

species.name: Black-crowned Night-Heron
species.about: A stocky heron that feeds mostly at dusk and night, often roosting in groups by day.

species.name: Cocoi Heron
species.about: The South American counterpart of the Great Blue Heron, with a black cap and a white neck.

species.name: Great Blue Heron
species.about: The largest heron in North America; it stalks fish in shallow water and flies with its neck folded into an S.

species.name: Great Egret
species.about: A tall, all-white heron with a yellow bill and black legs. Plume hunting nearly wiped it out around 1900.

species.name: Green Heron
species.about: A small, stocky heron that sometimes drops bait onto the water to lure fish, one of the few tool-using birds.

species.name: Snowy Egret
species.about: A slender white egret with a black bill and bright yellow feet that it uses to stir up prey.

species.name: Striated Heron
species.about: A small, widespread heron of the tropics, the close relative of the Green Heron.

species.name: Yellow-crowned Night-Heron
species.about: A crab specialist of coastal marshes, with a boldly striped black-and-white face.

species.name: Gilded Hummingbird
species.about: Also called the Gilded Sapphire: a coppery-gold hummingbird with a red bill and golden tail.

species.name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
species.about: The only hummingbird that breeds in the eastern US. Many cross the Gulf of Mexico nonstop on migration.

species.name: White-throated Hummingbird
species.about: A green hummingbird with a crisp white throat, common in gardens in southeastern South America.

species.name: Glossy Ibis
species.about: A dark wading bird with a long curved bill; its plumage glints green and maroon in good light.

species.name: Wattled Jacana
species.about: Walks on floating plants on very long toes. Males incubate the eggs and raise the chicks.

species.name: Belted Kingfisher
species.about: A shaggy-crested fish hunter with a rattling call. Unusually for birds, the female is the more colorful sex.

species.name: Ruby-crowned Kinglet
species.about: A tiny, restless olive bird that flicks its wings constantly; males hide a red crown patch.

species.name: Common Loon
species.about: A heavy-boned diving bird with a haunting yodel; it winters in gray plumage on coastal waters.

species.name: Brown Thrasher
species.about: A rufous songbird with one of the largest song repertoires of any North American bird.

species.name: Gray Catbird
species.about: A slate-gray mimic that mews like a cat and strings together borrowed phrases.

species.name: Northern Mockingbird
species.about: A tireless mimic that can learn hundreds of song types, and sometimes sings at night.

species.name: Dark-eyed Junco
species.about: A gray 'snowbird' that flashes white outer tail feathers; common in winter.

species.name: Eastern Towhee
species.about: A large sparrow that scratches noisily in leaf litter and sings 'drink-your-tea'.

species.name: Savannah Sparrow
species.about: A streaky grassland sparrow, often with a yellow wash above the eye.

species.name: Song Sparrow
species.about: A streaky sparrow with a central breast spot, and one of the most variable birds in North America.

species.name: White-throated Sparrow
species.about: Sings 'Old Sam Peabody, Peabody'. It comes in white-striped and tan-striped forms.

species.name: Turkey Vulture
species.about: A soaring scavenger that finds carrion by smell, flying with wings held in a teetering V.

species.name: American Redstart
species.about: Flashes orange or yellow tail patches to flush insects from foliage.

species.name: Black-and-white Warbler
species.about: Creeps along trunks and branches like a nuthatch, probing bark for insects.

species.name: Black-throated Blue Warbler
species.about: Males are deep blue with a black throat; females are olive, with a small white wing spot in both sexes.

species.name: Black-throated Green Warbler
species.about: A bright yellow face framing a black throat; sings a buzzy 'zee-zee-zoo-zoo-zee'.

species.name: Blackburnian Warbler
species.about: Males have a fiery orange throat; it forages high in conifers.

species.name: Chestnut-sided Warbler
species.about: A yellow-capped warbler with chestnut flanks that favors young, shrubby forest.

species.name: Common Yellowthroat
species.about: A skulking warbler of wet thickets; males wear a black bandit mask.

species.name: Magnolia Warbler
species.about: A yellow-and-black warbler with a distinctive tail pattern: white band near the base, black tip.

species.name: Northern Parula
species.about: A small blue-gray warbler with a yellow throat and a greenish patch on its back.

species.name: Northern Waterthrush
species.about: A streaky warbler that walks along the edges of water, bobbing its tail.

species.name: Ovenbird
species.about: A ground-walking warbler named for its domed nest; it sings a loud 'teacher-teacher-teacher'.

species.name: Palm Warbler
species.about: A ground-feeding warbler that constantly bobs its tail; an early spring migrant.

species.name: Southern Yellowthroat
species.about: A South American relative of the Common Yellowthroat; males have a black mask with a gray border.

species.name: Wilson's Warbler
species.about: A small yellow warbler; males wear a neat black cap.

species.name: Worm-eating Warbler
species.about: A plain warbler with bold head stripes that probes dead leaves for insects (not worms).

species.name: Yellow Warbler
species.about: An all-yellow warbler; males show chestnut streaks on the breast.

species.name: Yellow-rumped Warbler
species.about: One of the few warblers that can digest waxy berries, which lets it winter farther north than most.

species.name: Red-breasted Nuthatch
species.about: A small conifer nuthatch with a black eye stripe and a tinny 'yank-yank' call.

species.name: White-breasted Nuthatch
species.about: Creeps headfirst down tree trunks, wedging seeds into bark and hammering them open.

species.name: House Sparrow
species.about: An introduced, city-loving sparrow that is closely tied to human settlements worldwide.

species.name: Osprey
species.about: A fish-eating raptor that dives feet-first into water. Builds large stick nests on platforms, poles and channel markers.

species.name: Rufous Hornero
species.about: The national bird of Argentina; it builds a domed mud nest shaped like a clay oven.

species.name: Barred Owl
species.about: A brown-eyed forest owl known for its 'who cooks for you' call.

species.name: Burrowing Owl
species.about: A long-legged owl that lives in burrows in open grassland and is often active by day.

species.name: Eastern Screech-Owl
species.about: A small owl that roosts in tree cavities; comes in gray and rufous color morphs.

species.name: Eurasian Eagle-Owl
species.about: One of the largest owls in the world, with orange eyes and long ear tufts.

species.name: Great Horned Owl
species.about: A large, powerful owl with prominent ear tufts that nests earlier in the year than almost any other North American bird.

species.name: Snowy Owl
species.about: An Arctic owl that sometimes winters on beaches, airports and open fields far to the south.

species.name: Tropical Screech-Owl
species.about: A small, common owl of Latin American woodlands and city parks, with a purring trill.

species.name: American Oystercatcher
species.about: A shorebird with a bright orange bill built to pry open shellfish.

species.name: Maroon-bellied Parakeet
species.about: A green parakeet with a maroon belly patch and a long reddish tail, from Atlantic forests.

species.name: Monk Parakeet
species.about: The only parrot that builds stick nests. Feral colonies thrive in Brooklyn as well as in its native Argentina.

species.name: Ring-necked Pheasant
species.about: A long-tailed game bird from Asia, introduced widely; males have a white neck ring and red face wattles.

species.name: Mourning Dove
species.about: A slender dove with a soft, mournful coo; its wings whistle on takeoff.

species.name: Rock Pigeon
species.about: The city pigeon, descended from domesticated cliff-dwelling doves.

species.name: Killdeer
species.about: A plover that fakes a broken wing to lure predators away from its nest.

species.name: Piping Plover
species.about: A threatened, sand-colored plover that nests on open beaches, including the Rockaways.

species.name: Giant Wood-Rail
species.about: A large, loud rail of South American marshes, known for its raucous group choruses.

species.name: Greater Yellowlegs
species.about: A tall, active sandpiper with bright yellow legs and a ringing three-note call.

species.name: Sanderling
species.about: The little shorebird that chases the waves in and out along the beach.

species.name: Spotted Sandpiper
species.about: Teeters its tail constantly. Females defend territories while males incubate the eggs.

species.name: Black Skimmer
species.about: Flies low with its longer lower bill slicing the water and snaps it shut on fish.

species.name: European Starling
species.about: Released in Central Park in 1890, it now numbers in the tens of millions across North America.

species.name: Black-necked Stilt
species.about: A black-and-white shorebird with extraordinarily long pink legs.

species.name: Barn Swallow
species.about: A swallow with a deeply forked tail that builds mud nests on buildings and bridges.

species.name: Tree Swallow
species.about: An iridescent blue-green swallow that gathers in huge flocks on migration.

species.name: Double-collared Seedeater
species.about: A small seed-eating tanager; males have a black throat and a white band below it.

species.name: Golden-billed Saltator
species.about: A gray songbird with a bold white eyebrow and a bright orange-yellow bill.

species.name: Saffron Finch
species.about: A bright yellow, orange-crowned finch of open country; despite the name, it is a tanager.

species.name: American Robin
species.about: A familiar thrush that hunts earthworms on lawns; one of the first songs of the dawn chorus.

species.name: Eastern Bluebird
species.about: A blue-and-rust thrush of open country that readily uses nest boxes.

species.name: Hermit Thrush
species.about: A brown thrush with a reddish tail and an ethereal, flute-like song.

species.name: Rufous-bellied Thrush
species.about: The national bird of Brazil, a robin-like thrush with an orange belly.

species.name: Black-capped Chickadee
species.about: A tiny acrobat whose 'chick-a-dee' call carries more 'dees' when the threat is greater.

species.name: Tufted Titmouse
species.about: A gray, crested songbird with big dark eyes; a common feeder bird.

species.name: Eastern Kingbird
species.about: A black-and-white flycatcher that boldly chases hawks and crows away from its territory.

species.name: Eastern Phoebe
species.about: A tail-wagging flycatcher that calls its own name and often nests under bridges and eaves.

species.name: Great Crested Flycatcher
species.about: A cavity-nesting flycatcher with a lemon belly that often weaves shed snakeskin into its nest.

species.name: Great Kiskadee
species.about: A loud, bold flycatcher with a black-and-white masked head, named for its 'kis-ka-dee' call.

species.name: Say's Phoebe
species.about: A soft gray-brown flycatcher with a cinnamon belly, typical of dry open country in the West; like other phoebes, it constantly dips its tail while perched.

species.name: Cedar Waxwing
species.about: A sleek, crested fruit-eater named for the waxy red tips on its wing feathers.

species.name: Checkered Woodpecker
species.about: A small, finely barred woodpecker of South American open woodland.

species.name: Downy Woodpecker
species.about: The smallest North American woodpecker and a common feeder visitor.

species.name: Hairy Woodpecker
species.about: Looks like a larger Downy Woodpecker, with a much longer bill.

species.name: Northern Flicker
species.about: A woodpecker that often feeds on the ground, mostly on ants. Eastern birds flash yellow under the wings and tail.

species.name: Pileated Woodpecker
species.about: A crow-sized woodpecker with a flaming red crest that digs large rectangular holes in trees.

species.name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
species.about: A zebra-backed woodpecker with a red cap; the red belly that gives it its name is faint and hard to see.

species.name: Yellow-bellied Sapsucker
species.about: Drills neat rows of wells in tree bark and returns to feed on the sap and the insects it attracts.

species.name: Carolina Wren
species.about: A small but very loud wren whose 'teakettle-teakettle' song carries for a long way.

species.name: House Wren
species.about: A plain brown wren with a bubbly song that nests in almost any cavity.

species.name: Southern House Wren
species.about: The South American form of the House Wren, common around homes and gardens.
